text.lead:
Peace, Love & Misunderstanding is a 2011 American comedy-drama film directed by Bruce Beresford and starring Jane Fonda, Catherine Keener, Jeffrey Dean Morgan, Elizabeth Olsen, Nat Wolff, Chace Crawford, Kyle MacLachlan, and Rosanna Arquette. It was filmed in the town of Woodstock, New York, the same town in which the film is set.
Manhattan lawyer Diane heads upstate with her NYC teens to Woodstock to stay with her estranged hippie mother after her husband demands a divorce, where they all change their life perspectives: poetry-reading Zoe becomes interested in the sensitive young butcher Cole, nerdy Jake gathers material for his first film project, and Diane herself grows close with carpenter/singer Jude. Most importantly, Diane finally ends the decades-long war with her mother.
The film had a gala premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 13, 2011. It was released to theaters on June 8, 2012, starting in limited release. It was released on DVD and Blu-ray Disc on October 2, 2012.
text.plot:
Manhattan lawyer Diane's husband Mark demands a divorce, just their dinner party with friends begins. Quietly devastated, she sits silently through the evening. Later, Diane announces she and their two teens are heading to Woodstock to stay with her estranged hippie mother, so Mark insists they sign the divorce papers on her return.
Driving to the charming village in silence, Diane tells Zoe and Jake the news upon arriving at Grace's. Her daughter Zoe is shocked, as she has been at Columbia. However, Jake expresses relief, as he has been witnessing their fighting.
Entering the Bohemian home, with chickens wandering freely inside, they pass through a bead curtain. There they find the hippie Grace at her pottery wheel. She tells them she dreamed about their coming. Not having seen each other for 20 years, the stiff Diane lets her mother hug her.
Later, inside, Zoe ask questions based on what she sees in the house. Filming, Jake asks questions as he is working on a project. It soon becomes evident that Diane is politically conservative, while her mother is the complete opposite.
Diane has yet to reveal why she suddenly broke the 20-year silence between her and Grace, who expresses her gratitude for visiting. As they talk, Diane requests that her mother refrain from her usual activities, in regards to men specifically. Grace promises to be on her best behavior.
On Saturday, the four head downtown, where Grace participates in a weekly anti-war protest. At the first opportunity, Diane extracts herself, Zoe, and Jake from the demonstration to go shopping, eventually entering a butcher's shop. Zoe is appalled, being a vegetarian. Cole is the butcher, who explains he does his best to be organic and responsible.
Her city kids get a new perspective on life: poetry-reading daughter Zoe becomes interested in a sensitive young butcher Cole, nerdy son Jake finds material for his first film project, and Diane herself grows close to a handsome carpenter/singer Jude. Most importantly, Diane finally gets the chance to end the ancient war with the mother she has not seen for two decades.

- Joyce Van Patten as Mariam
- Katharine McPhee as Sara

text.reception: Peace, Love & Misunderstanding received negative reviews from critics. As of June 2020, the film holds a 30% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, based on 70 reviews with an average rating of 4.7 out of 10. The website's critics consensus reads: " Peace, Love, & Misunderstanding produces many unintentional laughs with its absurdly contrived plot and cheery insistence that everything is just super".
